title.value: What does it mean to be a responsible AI practitioner: An ontology of roles and skills
title.justification: The paper focuses on defining roles and skills necessary for responsible AI practitioners, hence the title reflects this purpose.
title.quote: In this work, we examine what responsible AI practitioners do in the industry and what skills they employ on the job. We propose an ontology of existing roles alongside skills and competencies that serve each role.

extractions.description: The paper explores the roles and skills of responsible AI practitioners. It develops an ontology that outlines the roles, responsibilities, skills, and qualifications needed for these practitioners, based on job postings and expert interviews. This work is intended to help industry leaders build responsible AI teams and to assist educators in developing AI ethics curricula.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not specifically address any of the listed eco-responsible categories such as Climate Change Mitigation, Adaptation, or Pollution. Instead, it deals with AI ethics and responsible AI practices, focusing on roles and skills required in this emerging field.
primary_category.quote: Our ontology contributes to business leaders looking to build responsible AI teams and provides educators with a set of competencies that an AI ethics curriculum can prioritize.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper is centered around AI ethics and education, without a direct link to environmental sustainability or eco-responsible AI.
secondary_categories.quote: With the growing need to regulate AI systems across a wide variety of application domains, a new set of occupations has emerged in the industry. The so-called responsible Artificial Intelligence (AI) practitioners or AI ethicists are generally tasked with interpreting and operationalizing best practices for ethical and safe design of AI systems.

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit into any of the specific eco-responsible sub-categories provided. It primarily addresses the development of roles and skills for responsible AI practice.
primary_sub_category.quote: We propose an ontology of existing roles alongside skills and competencies that serve each role. We created this ontology by examining the job postings for such roles over a two-year period (2020-2022) and conducting expert interviews with fourteen individuals who currently hold such a role in the industry.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: Given its focus on responsible AI and ethics roles, the paper does not align with any eco-responsible sub-categories listed.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: We discuss how educators and employers can use this competency framework to develop new curricula/programs and adequately recruit for the rapidly changing field of responsible AI development.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper is primarily concerned with the roles, skills, and educational needs in AI ethics, which is not covered by the existing categories. It addresses how to train AI practitioners to responsibly engage with AI ethics.
new_primary_category.quote: Our ontology contributes to business leaders looking to build responsible AI teams and provides educators with a set of competencies that an AI ethics curriculum can prioritize.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The paper specifically investigates the roles and skills of responsible AI practitioners, which is a new niche within AI ethics that is not covered by existing sub-categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: We find that the ability to work in an interdisciplinary environment, communicate and engage with diverse stakeholder groups, and the aptitude for curiosity and self-learning are consistently highlighted for all of the roles.
